\begin{theorem}[Inner enumeration counting invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.guloop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.guloop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.GS, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wb, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wt, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_spec, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.choose, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₃_neg, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₃_pos}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be
an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$
be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, write $R(u,v)$ for the assertion that the
type-$3$ query encoding $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ returns true, and write $I(u)$ for the
assertion that the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$ returns true. Define
$\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)$ to mean that some $u<\sigma.K$ with $I(u)$ reaches $t$ in at
most $\sigma.i$ steps of $R$. Let $\operatorname{GS}(A,B_0,C;r,t,c)$ be the recursive
predicate that at depth zero requires $C(c)$, and at each positive depth either requires
$A(t)$ and recurses with $t+1,c+1$, or requires $B_0(t)$ and recurses with $t+1,c$.
Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.K+1\le B$,
$\sigma.u\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.cnt\le\sigma.u$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=0$.
If, whenever $\operatorname{GS}$ holds at depth $\sigma.K-\sigma.u$, position
$\sigma.u$, count $\sigma.cnt$, with first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_i(t)\land
t\ne\sigma.v\land\neg R(t,\sigma.v)$, second predicate always true, and terminal
condition $c=\sigma.cp$, the machine at state $\mathrm{vn}$ with $u=cnt=0$ terminates
within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine at state
$\mathrm{uh}$ with registers $\sigma$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts
exactly when that recursive condition holds together with $Q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Outer enumeration invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gvloop}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gvloop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.GS, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Clear, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wb, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.wt, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.gs_and, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.guloop, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gwalk_spec, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.choose, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₂_neg, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_call₂_pos}
\difficulty{7}
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be
an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\operatorname{Kont}:\mathbb
N\to\mathrm{Prop}$, and let $\sigma$ be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, let
$R(u,v)$ and $I(u)$ denote respectively the truth of the type-$3$ query encoding
$(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ and the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$, and let
$\operatorname{Mem}_j(t)$ mean that some $I$-witness below $\sigma.K$ reaches $t$ in at
most $j$ steps of $R$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.K+1\le
B$, $\sigma.v\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.c\le\sigma.v$, and
$\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$. Assume that for every
$c'\le\sigma.K$, if the outer recursive condition holds from position $\sigma.v$, count
$\sigma.c$, and depth $\sigma.K-\sigma.v$, with terminal condition $c=c'$, then the
stage-end machine initialized with $v=K,c=c'$ terminates within register bound $B$ and
accepts exactly when $\operatorname{Kont}(c')$ holds. The outer condition uses first
predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_{i1}(t)\land\neg\operatorname{AccO}(t)$ and second
predicate given by the inner recursive condition of depth $K$, starting at position and
count zero, with first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_i(u)\land u\ne t\land\neg R(u,t)$,
second predicate always true, and terminal condition count $\sigma.cp$. Then the machine
initialized at the outer-enumeration test state with registers $\sigma$ terminates
within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when the outer recursive condition holds
with terminal predicate $\operatorname{Kont}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Stage enumeration invariant]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gstage}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gstage}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.GS, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.Mem, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.RelO, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Bd, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.St.Clear, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.ball, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.gs_inner, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.gs_outer, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.not_mem_succ_iff, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rc, Complexity.LogProg.ISCount.rcp, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.IG.of_eq, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.St.greg, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.gvloop, Complexity.LogProg.ISGen.igA, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.clr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy}
\difficulty{6}
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{0,1\}$ be
an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$
be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, write $R(u,v)$ for the assertion that the
oracle returns true on the type-$3$ query encoding $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$; write $I(u)$ for
the assertion that it returns true on the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$; and
let $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ be the set of numbers below $\sigma.K$ reachable from some
$I$-witness by at most $j$ steps of $R$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most
$B$, $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.i\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.i1=\sigma.i+1$,
$\sigma.cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_{\sigma.i}|$, and
$\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$. If, for all $v',c'\le B$, the
comparison-stage machine initialized with $i=K$, $i1=K+1$, $v=v'$, $c=c'$, and
$cp=|\operatorname{Ball}_K|$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts
exactly when $Q$ holds, then the stage-head machine initialized in state $\sigma$
terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds and no
member of $\operatorname{Ball}_j$ is accepted by the type-$2$ oracle query for any $j$
with $\sigma.i<j\le\sigma.K$.
\end{theorem}
